builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right
summary: Soft-MTP replaces the standard multi-token prediction cross-entropy gradient with only its KL self-distillation component, recovered exactly by combining existing NTP and MTP cross-entropy gradients via straight-through routing, implemented as a one-line code change. It costs no additional parameters, memory, or compute, and avoids the vocabulary-sized logit matrices required by direct KL minimization. It can fail in that all evidence comes from pre-training runs up to 1.2B parameters, so the benefit is unverified at production model scales and only applies to teams that run their own pre-training with MTP heads.
rationale: The technique is a pre-training modification, and the reader has no capacity for foundation-model training, so it is relevant only as something to watch for adoption in open-weight models rather than to deploy directly.
technique: Soft-MTP: KL gradient-recovery for multi-token prediction

claims.statement: Soft-MTP replaces the standard multi-token prediction cross-entropy gradient with only its KL self-distillation component, recovered exactly by combining existing NTP and MTP cross-entropy gradients via straight-through routing, implemented as a one-line code change. It costs no additional parameters, memory, or compute, and avoids the vocabulary-sized logit matrices required by direct KL minimization. It can fail in that all evidence comes from pre-training runs up to 1.2B parameters, so the benefit is unverified at production model scales and only applies to teams that run their own pre-training with MTP heads.

Soft-MTP improves over standard MTP at every scale from 167M to 1.2B parameters, with lower next-token perplexity, faster speculative decoding, higher zero-shot accuracy, and stronger math and code reasoning after fine-tuning at 1.2B, with no measurable overhead.
